bib.title: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2024 (38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); arXiv v5, 19 Jan 2025

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only. Figure plots (4, 5, 6, 8-11, 13-20) are extracted as axis numbers only, so curve values are not readable.

question: How can queries be routed between black-box LMs of different sizes so that a user gets the best cost-quality tradeoff without fine-tuning a router on large task-specific data?
hypothesis: A small LM's few-shot, context-grounded self-verification is a noisy but useful signal of answer correctness, and a POMDP router that treats it as a noisy observation of question difficulty routes better than trained routers (FrugalGPT, HybridLLM).
contributions: Few-shot self-verification framed as context-entailment, needing no verifier training
POMDP-based router that handles noisy verifier outputs, learns from as few as 50 examples and generalises to N>2 models
Incremental Benefit per Cost (IBC) metric for comparing model-mixing methods

method.summary: The small LM generates an answer, the same small LM verifies it against the context by sampling several few-shot Correct/Incorrect judgements (verifier probability = fraction judged Correct), and a router (threshold or POMDP trained on a small labelled set) decides whether to keep the answer or call a larger LM. Evaluated on five context-grounded tasks with Mistral-7B, LLaMA2-13B or GPT-3.5 as the small model and GPT-4 as the large one, with simulated relative costs; also a 3-model setup with LLaMA2-70B in the middle.
method.task: context-grounded QA and dialogue reasoning with model routing (cost-performance tradeoff)

datasets.preprocessing: context subset max 3500 tokens retrieved with the question as key using all-MiniLM-L6-v2

datasets.name: CoQA
datasets.source: Reddy et al. 2019; multiple licences per split
datasets.preprocessing: same retrieval, max 3500 tokens; QUALITY prompt adapted

datasets.name: MuTual
datasets.preprocessing: same retrieval, max 3500 tokens; QUALITY prompt adapted

datasets.name: DIPLOMAT
datasets.preprocessing: same retrieval, max 3500 tokens; QUALITY prompt adapted

other.role_detail: small LM (SLM), relative cost 1 unit; LLM GPT-4 costs 200
SLM, relative cost 1; GPT-4 costs 100. Hosted with vllm from huggingface

models.name: AutoMix router (threshold / POMDP)
models.architecture: threshold on verifier probability v (return SLM answer if v >= t), or POMDP with KDE observation model and AdaOps solver

other.solver: AdaOps (Wu et al. 2021); a simpler tree search with particle filtering is also described and said to converge to about the same solution

models.name: FrugalGPT router
models.architecture: fine-tuned DistilBERT router; threshold on confidence

models.name: HybridLLM router
models.architecture: trained DeBERTa router choosing SLM or LLM directly; labels from probability SLM outperforms LLM by a margin over multiple samples

inference.decoding: greedy (temperature 0), single sample for both SLM and LLM answers
inference.temperature: 0 for answers; verification temperature printed as 1 in Appendix B first paragraph and 0.7 in Appendix B Datasets paragraph (and 'high' in Sec 4.1)
inference.samples: 1 sample per answer; 8 verification samples per question; seeds/repeats not stated
inference.prompting: Task prompt from Shaham et al. 2023 (QASPER, QUALITY), QUALITY prompt adapted for CoQA/MuTual/DIPLOMAT; identical prompts for all models. Verifier: one generic few-shot prompt for all tasks, printed as 4-shot in Sec 4.1 and 3-shot in Listing 4 caption (two examples visible plus truncated examples).
inference.retrieval: context truncated to max 3500 tokens by retrieval with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 using the question as key

parameters.verifier_cost: C_ver = C_SLM; total C = C_SLM + C_ver + w*C_LLM; 8 verifier samples counted as one call
parameters.cost_regions: dIBC averaged over five equally sized cost regions

other.pomdp_latency: less than 1ms per query in two-model setup
other.api_prices_quoted: $0.225 for LLAMA2-13B vs $30 for GPT-4 per 1M tokens (ratio stated as 1:100, written 'between GPT-4 and GPT-4' in the appendix)
other.hardware_hint: A6000 GPU mentioned only as an example scenario

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: answer F1 on QASPER and CoQA

metrics.name: Incremental Benefit per Cost (IBC)
metrics.definition: IBC_M = (P_M - P_SLM)/(C_M - C_SLM); IBC_BASE = (P_LLM - P_SLM)/(C_LLM - C_SLM)

metrics.name: dIBC
metrics.definition: (IBC_M - IBC_BASE)/IBC_BASE * 100, averaged over five equally sized cost regions

baselines: N=3: FrugalGPT cascade, Union AutoMix, Chained AutoMix
eval.protocol: 1000 sampled validation instances per dataset; router trained on a labelled train/validation split whose default size is not stated (size swept 50 to 1000 in Fig 5); no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported for Table 1; training baselines and AutoMix requires inference on all models (training-time cost only).

prompts.text: Context: The manuscript, discovered in 1980 in a dusty attic, turned out to be a lost work of Shakespeare. Question: Whose lost work was discovered in a dusty attic in 1980? AI Generated Answer: Shakespeare ... Evaluation: The context specifically mentions that a lost work of Shakespeare was discovered in 1980 in a dusty attic. Verification Decision: The AI generated answer is Correct.

Context: The celestial event, known as the Pink Moon, is unique to the month of April and has cultural significance in many indigenous tribes. Question: In which month does the celestial event, the Pink Moon, occur? AI Generated Answer: July ... Evaluation: The context clearly states that the Pink Moon is unique to the month of April. Verification Decision: The AI generated answer is Incorrect.

results.claim: AutoMix reduces computational cost by over 50% at comparable performance (headline; no table gives the percentage directly, support is the cost-performance curves and dIBC).
results.setup: Five datasets, small LMs Mistral-7B/LLaMA2-13B/GPT-3.5 with GPT-4 as LLM, simulated relative costs 1 vs 60/100/200, verifier cost counted for AutoMix and zero for baseline routers.
results.quote: reducing computational cost by over 50% for comparable performance.
results.note: Intro says 'reducing cost by over two times while achieving the same performance'. Abstract also counts 'five language models' (Mistral-7B, LLaMA2-13B, GPT-3.5, LLaMA2-70B, GPT-4).

results.claim: With Mistral-7B as SLM, AutoMix+POMDP dIBC ranges from 12.4% (CoQA) to 156.8% (DIPLOMAT) and exceeds FrugalGPT and HybridLLM on all five datasets.
results.setup: Mistral-7B SLM, GPT-4 LLM, cost ratio 1:200, DIPLOMAT, averaged over five equal cost regions; baseline_value is FrugalGPT on DIPLOMAT (HybridLLM 67.1).
results.table: Table 1, rows MISTRAL-7B AutoMix + P, column DIPLOMAT (CoQA 12.4, MUTUAL 46.7, QASPER 69.3, QUALITY 51.6; FrugalGPT 16.8 20.3 -16.7 7.7 8.1; HybridLLM 67.1 3.4 10.5 0.4 2.7)

results.claim: AutoMix+POMDP is the only method with positive dIBC in every configuration and matches or exceeds AutoMix+Threshold.
results.setup: Table 1, three SLMs x five datasets.
results.quote: AutoMix-POMDP is the only method that yields positive gains across all configurations and consistently matches or exceeds the performance of AutoMix-Threshold.
results.note: Table 1 shows AutoMix+T above AutoMix+P in 2 of 15 cells (GPT-3.5 DIPLOMAT 168.2 vs 151.2; LLaMA2-13B CoQA 86.5 vs 83.1), so 'consistently matches or exceeds' is loose; AutoMix+T has -0.2 for LLaMA2-13B QASPER, so only POMDP is positive everywhere.

results.claim: Text says AutoMix-POMDP outperforms FrugalGPT on all datasets and models, 'equalling' it on QASPER for LLaMA2-13B, but Table 1 shows FrugalGPT higher there.
results.setup: LLaMA2-13B SLM, GPT-4 LLM, QASPER; baseline is FrugalGPT.
results.table: Table 1, row LLAMA2-13B AutoMix + P, column QASPER (FrugalGPT 9.4)

results.claim: Best dIBC gains are on DIPLOMAT, averaging 122% across all models.
results.quote: with the best performance observed on the DIPLOMAT dataset, averaging 122% across all models.
results.note: From Table 1 AutoMix+P on DIPLOMAT: 156.8, 58.5, 151.2 gives mean 122.2.

results.claim: With only 50 training examples AutoMix keeps 15% dIBC and beats the baselines by more than 20% absolute.
results.setup: Fig 5 left; train size swept 50 to 1000; baselines FrugalGPT and HybridLLM trained on same data with zero router cost. SLM and datasets for the macro average not stated in caption.
results.quote: with just 50 training examples, AutoMix maintains 15% ∆IBC and beats the baselines by more than absolute 20%.
results.note: Appendix A.3 says FrugalGPT narrows the gap as training data grows.

results.claim: Out-of-domain (router trained on one dataset, tested on other four) AutoMix averages 28.3 / 31.5 / 70.9 dIBC for Mistral-7B / LLaMA2-13B / GPT-3.5, vs FrugalGPT 12.5 / 0.0 / 14.3 and HybridLLM 2.4 / -2.8 / 7.6.
results.setup: Mistral-7B column shown; each of five datasets used once as training set, evaluated on other four; 3 SLMs.
results.table: Table 5, row Automix, column Mistral-7b (LLama-13b 31.5, GPT-3.5 70.9)
results.note: Table unit not printed; assumed dIBC. Layout in the text extraction lists values per row.

results.claim: Even at a cost ratio as low as 1:10, AutoMix starts to deliver good gains on many datasets.
results.setup: Fig 5 right, dIBC normalised by max value per dataset.
results.quote: even for a cost ratio as low as 1:10, AutoMix begins to deliver good gains for many datasets
results.note: Appendix B says 'even with a ratio as low as 1:25' and D.2 says at 20:1 AutoMix still outperforms baselines with smaller margins; ratios disagree across sections.

results.claim: POMDP inference takes less than 1ms per query and adds no meaningful latency.
results.setup: Two-model setup; network latency about 10ms; SLM/LLM generation on the order of seconds. Hardware not stated.
results.quote: At inference time, POMDP takes less than 1ms for every query in the two-model setup.
results.note: Appendix A.3.1 says policies are learned offline so POMDP is a lookup table at inference.

results.claim: In 13 of 15 configurations AutoMix-POMDP is clearly better than all baselines across operating costs; in the other 2 it is competitive.
results.quote: for 13/15 configurations, AutoMix-POMDP is clearly better than all other baselines throughout different operating costs.

results.claim: In the 3-model setup (LLaMA2-13B, LLaMA2-70B, GPT-4) AutoMix beats FrugalGPT, Union AutoMix and Chained AutoMix across cost regions in representative cases, but gives no significant gain in two cases where MLM self-verification is poor.
results.setup: Figs 6, 8-11, 13-17; numeric curve values not readable from extracted text.
results.quote: In previous subsections, we considered cases, where AutoMix was significantly better than FrugalGPT and often the other variants of AutoMix.

results.claim: Verifier probability tracks correctness for all datasets except QUALITY and QASPER (and QASPER mostly holds apart from 2/9 outliers).
results.metric: precision of correct answers by verifier-probability bin
results.setup: LLaMA2-13B as SLM; correct defined as F1 > 0.1 (Fig 12).
results.quote: For all but QUALITY and QASPER higher verification probability, always higher precision.
results.note: Appendix text says 'for all but once' in the preceding sentence.

limits: Authors concede AutoMix is designed for context-grounded / dialogue reasoning where the context allows verification; it does not cover factual QA or commonsense reasoning.
Costs are simulated relative units from API price ratios (1 vs 60/100/200), not measured spend or latency; baseline routers are charged 0 while AutoMix pays for verification.

Only GPT-4 is used as the large model; evaluation on 1000-instance samples; no seeds, intervals or significance tests for Table 1; default router training set size, lambda, KDE bandwidth and particle count are not stated.
N=3 experiments show cases with no significant gain when the middle model's self-verification is uninformative (Fig 11).
Prices and model versions (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Mistral-7B v0.2) have dated; authors note cheaper strong models may make serving one strong model feasible.
Task generalisation to generation tasks with subjective performance is left as future work.

terms.definition: IBC_M = (P_M - P_SLM)/(C_M - C_SLM): slope on the performance-cost plot from the SLM point to the method's point; dIBC compares it with the SLM-to-LLM slope.
the small model judges, as an entailment task, whether its answer is consistent with the context; probability is the fraction of k samples judged correct.

code.snippet: procedure ANSWERQUERY(C, q): As <- SOLVE(SLM, C, q); v <- SELF-VERIFY(As, C, q); if META-VERIFY(v, As, C, q) then return As else Al <- SOLVE(LLM, C, q); return Al
